headline: AlphaFold and Foldseek models expand structure-based binding-site and fold annotation
label: Structural Protein Resource Curation
summary: Structure predictions and standardized, cross-linked resources now enable large-scale reuse of protein structure and binding annotations.
synthesis: The dominant thread is the combination of predicted structures with curated, cross-linked annotation. OpenAntigens provides a free, no-login database of construct-design reports for 5328 human cell-surface and secreted proteins, integrating UniProt, AlphaFold, PDB, and related data. The two preprints are computational workflows rather than resources. One scans AlphaFold models of human membrane-associated proteins for structure-based polyphosphate binding surfaces. The other uses ESMFold predictions and Foldseek/TM-align searches to assign a Ly-6/uPAR three-finger fold to a leech salivary EV protein and to flag an unresolved structurally dark fraction. What is new is the scale and standardization of structure-derived data for reuse. The database entries do not report a shared computational method, so the common thread is data curation rather than a single approach.
